subject: fennec
pitch: A fennec fox kit standing alert on a little sand dune at dusk. Enormous satin ears lined in pale peach, cream fur warming to sandy gold along its back, a fluffy tail with a smudge of black at the tip, and big dark eyes with a tiny white sparkle. Its paws are a touch oversized, like it hasn't grown into them yet, and it wears a woven leather collar with a small brass bell.
reasoning:
I'm planning a stylized fennec fox kit standing atop a dune, working out proportions for the body, head, and oversized ears relative to a 0.2m shoulder height, with the dune serving as the base platform at y=0.

Now I'm sketching the joint hierarchy in code — setting ground level, hip height, and leg length, then defining the spine chain from hips through chest with specific coordinates for each vertebra.

Defining leg chains next...

Adding a few lighter toe bumps per paw to keep things subtle. For the body I'm planning a loft along the spine with countershading paint—sandy on top, cream underneath, blended using the surface normal—and setting up rump station dimensions as the starting point.

Continuing the loft stations up the spine toward the shoulders, then deciding to rig it with a chain bone setup since the SDK should handle that even with moderate uncertainty around knot counts. After that I'm placing the neck and head joints to prep for building the head geometry.

Still working out jaw and eye positioning...

Now I'm thinking about dark tear-line markings beneath the eyes for the fennec look, then moving to the oversized ears — planning an extruded outline shape with points defining the width and height curve to get that tall, pointed ear silhouette.

I'm scaling the inner ear outline and setting up joint positions for earL/earTipL with bend tilt vectors, then mirroring the outward tilt for the right ear by flipping the x-component of the y-vector so normals still face forward symmetrically.

Head top sits around y=0.325 with ear bases sunk slightly in at y=0.305, giving the kit a total height near 0.45 once ears are included, which feels proportionate for a fennec-style fox. I'm also planning cream cone spikes along the cheeks for fur ruff, placing a few per side pointing outward and back from the head bone.

Now I'm working out the tail: a chain swept along a curved path from the rump down and back, built from four tapering segments with radii shrinking toward the tip, colored with a gradient that shifts from sandy to cream and darkens to black at the very end.

Now I'm working out the collar: a torus ringed around the neck in leather brown, oriented along the neck's tilt axis, sized small with a thin tube radius, and considering small stitch-like boxes looped around it for texture.

Still wiring up the weave geometry...

Now I need to figure out where the brass bell sits on the collar—computing the outward-facing direction perpendicular to the neck axis so it hangs at the front-bottom.

I'm also sizing the neck as a capsule between the joint positions, sharing the same countershade paint pattern as the body for visual consistency.

For the coat paint itself, I'm blending cream and sand tones based on height and surface normal to create a countershading effect, with some noise added for mottling and lighter tones around the muzzle and cheeks. I'm keeping this approach consistent across all meshes to manage the chart/paint cost reasonably.

Now I'm shifting to the legs, fading sandy outer color to cream paws based on vertical position, with the cream kicking in below a certain height threshold, and considering tiny dark claws. I'm also sketching out the dune shape as a lathe geometry, defining the outline points that control its radius and height profile.

I'll add striped grain texture to the sand, then shape the dune with a smooth lathe and maybe a second smaller mound for an elongated look. For bone structure, I'm thinking the dune should ride on a root joint, with "hips" as a child bone, keeping everything anchored to a single root at the origin.

Now I'm checking proportions—dune radius needs shrinking to about 0.38 to match the fox's scale properly. For the whiskers, I'm sketching thin rods extending from the muzzle with a cream color, three per side, and starting to define the leg joint function with position offsets for front versus back legs.

Defining more joint points...

Still defining joints...

Checking paw sphere positioning against ground height so the grooves sit right at the top surface without sinking in, and noting that the dune's lathe profile actually slopes down away from center, so I need to account for that curvature near the feet rather than assuming a flat ground plane.

Now I'm adding forward-pointing cream spikes at the chest to form a fluffy ruff, and working out the tail's base thickness and path, sweeping it from the rump using a catmull-rom spline through a few joint points so it tapers naturally along the body.

Setting up the tail bone chain with four joints parented to the hips, then defining a tapering sweep radius profile so it thickens near the base and narrows toward a rounded tip. For the head, I'm adding cheek ruff spikes using explicit base points and direction vectors, then placing a dark capsule stripe running from the inner eye corner down toward the muzzle to form a tear mark.

Working out stripe placement...

I'll make the muzzle a scaled sphere with a small nose sphere on top, and sketch a lower jaw as another scaled sphere near the chin, keeping proportions compact and cream-colored.

For the eyes, I'm computing where they sit on the head's ellipsoid surface so they're embedded correctly, giving them a dark iris color and a small white sparkle positioned toward the upper outer edge for a glossy highlight.

Adding three small cream tufts near each ear's inner base, positioning them forward of the ear plane and setting up the extrusion geometry with a sandy paint color for the ear's outer surface.

Still defining ear geometry...

Adding darker golden ruff coloring along the back for fennec-style features, then setting up a reasonable paint texture size and a helper function for placing geometry parts with position, scale, and bone bindings.

I'm checking whether the collar ring, positioned partway up the neck capsule, would intersect with the back of the head geometry -- working through the coordinate math to make sure the collar sits clear of the head's lower-back curve.

Since the collar's front-bottom point still falls inside the chest cap's radius, I'm shifting the neck segment further forward and up to give the collar more clearance, then recomputing the distance from the chest center to confirm it's finally outside the body surface.

Still working out collar box geometry...

Writing material and paint code...

Still defining paint functions...

Now I'm working out the chain helper for legs and spine, setting up polyline paths with named joints like shoulder/elbow/wrist/paw for the front legs and hip/knee/hock/paw for the hind legs, each tagged with side suffixes.

Writing capsule radii and whiskers...

I'm placing small lathed mounds at the dune edges, outside the main dune radius so they extend it naturally without poking through, then wrapping up the answer.
